content: The test image shows a corn ear with yellow kernels heavily covered in dark blue-green to gray-green mold, with some white areas. This is a pod/seed affected plant part. Top candidates: Trichoderma_Ear_Rot (blue-green conidia from base to middle), Aspergillus_Ear_Rot (olive-green powdery mold at tip), or Diplodia_Ear_Rot (white mycelium from base).

The reference Trichoderma image shows green-black speckling on husks. The test image shows the exposed ear with gray-green mold broadly covering kernels across most of the ear, with some white areas near the top.

Comparing to the symptom descriptions:
- **Trichoderma**: "dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels; white mycelium on husk leaves turning green to gray-green; typically from base to middle of cob covering all kernels" — matches the broad coverage and color well
- **Aspergillus**: olive-green powdery mold typically starting at the tip only — doesn't match the broad coverage
- **Diplodia**: white mycelium from base — not matching the green color

The broad gray-green mold coverage across the entire ear with some white areas is most consistent with Trichoderma_Ear_Rot.
